# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 1 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 1
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Greetings, sons and daughters, in the name of the Lord who loved us, in peace.
2. Since God's righteous ordinances are great and rich toward you, I rejoice exceedingly and beyond measure over your blessed and glorious spirits — so innate is the grace of the spiritual gift you have received.
3. Therefore I myself also congratulate myself the more that I am hoping to be saved; because I truly see in you the Spirit poured out upon you from the rich Lord of love.
4. Thus the long-hoped-for vision of you has struck me, and I am persuaded of it.
5. Being therefore convinced of this, and being conscious that after speaking many things among you I know that the Lord traveled with me on the road of righteousness; I am under all constraint also to love you above my own soul — because great faith and love dwells in you, in the hope of his life.
6. Reasoning therefore that if I take care to communicate to you some portion of what I received, it will turn out to my reward that I served such souls — I hastened to send you a short letter, so that alongside your faith you may have perfect knowledge.
7. There are then three doctrines of the Lord: the hope of life — which is the beginning and end of our faith; and righteousness — which is the beginning and end of judgment; and love of joy and gladness — testimony to works of righteousness.
8. For the Master made known to us through the prophets things past and things present, and has given us the first-fruits of the taste of things to come; and seeing each of these things coming to pass as he said, we ought to offer a richer and loftier offering to the fear of him.
9. But I will show you a few things, not as a teacher but as one of your own — a few things by which you will be glad in the present circumstances.
